title: The Table
location: Pune. Your parents' flat. Diwali week, 8 p.m.
architect_intro: Dinner. Your mother has told him. He has decided she hasn't.
player_goal: Leave for London with your father's understanding, or at least without breaking the table.
stated_objection: London. Fine. Go. Everyone goes. Who will remember the old man.

hidden_objection_layers.text: He believes the practice was worth nothing if no one wants it.

objects.label: Photograph on the sideboard
objects.reveals_text: Face-down. When you turn it in your mind you know it: Aajoba, his father, in a Nehru cap.

objects.label: Cassette player
objects.reveals_text: Bal Gandharva, 'Natya Sangeet Vol. 2'. The case is held together with Sellotape.

objects.label: Pickle jar
objects.reveals_text: His lime pickle. He made it in March. It's closed. He hasn't offered it.

t1.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t1.line: Eat. You're thin. They don't have proper food there, only sandwiches. [Pause.] London, London. Fine. Go. Everyone goes. Who will remember the old man.

tells.anchor: phrase:Who will remember the old man.
tells.reading: A bid for recognition, wearing a joke.
tells.false_positive: It's a joke. He makes this joke at every wedding.

choices.text: Baba, it's a really good job. It's the right move for my career.

rebuttal.text: Career. Career is a word for people who don't have a business.

choices.text: Tell me about the first client. I never actually heard it properly.
None of what I've got would exist without you, Baba. You're the reason I'm good at anything.
choices.note: Truthful=false: the flight is already booked and this is being said to end the conversation.

choices.text: [say nothing; serve yourself rice]

t2.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t2.line: Career. Career is a word for people who don't have a business. [He tears a chapati in half, puts both halves down.] Your mother says the salary is very good. Good. Very good.

tells.false_positive: His teeth. He's been complaining about a molar.

choices.text: Baba, look at the numbers. The practice has been shrinking for four years.
I'm sorry. That came out like I was selling you something. Can I ask about the practice instead?
[say nothing]

t3.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t3.line: First client. Bhide sir. Bhide Electricals, 1990. He paid me in a cheque that bounced. [He almost smiles.] Then the flood, 1997. Water to the first step. I carried the files up myself. Your mother carried you. You were this big. You slept on the ledgers.

tells.reading: The practice and you are the same story to him.

choices.text: I learned to read a balance sheet at this table. That came from you.
Was it what you wanted? Accountancy?
Bhide sir. Does he still come?

t4.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t4.line: [He reaches for the pickle jar, stops, puts it back.] Your mother made the shrikhand. Take. [He hums two lines of something, Bal Gandharva, off-key.] Thirty-four years. Two rooms above a sweet shop.

tells.reading: He made it for you. He's not giving it to you.

choices.text: Can I have the pickle, Baba?
Thirty-four years. What would happen to it, if no one took it on?

t5.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t5.line: [He pushes the pickle across without looking.] Bhide sir died in 2019. His son comes. The son thinks GST is a type of yoga. [He laughs once.] So. London.

choices.text: London. I'm going, Baba. I'm not asking you to like it. I'm asking you to help me with something nobody else will do right.
What would make it easier for you?

line_by_state.line: [Long silence. He looks at the sideboard. At the face-down photograph.] My father wanted me in accountancy. I wanted engineering. COEP. I had the letter. He took it from the post. [Pause.] I said I'd never do that. And I made the board say '& Co.' for twenty years, waiting. What is it worth, if nobody wants it. Tell me. Ramu, enough.

tells.reading: His mother's name for him. He's said too much.
tells.false_positive: He talks to himself. Always has.

choices.text: It was worth me. And Bhide's son. And eleven people who still call you sir. I'm going, Baba. And I need you for one thing. My tax residency. Two countries. You're the only one I trust to do it.
You did the same thing he did. You know that, right?
Okay. I'll eat.

t7.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t7.line: Tax residency. [Scoff.] They'll make a mess. Non-resident rules, DTAA, the hundred-and-eighty-two days. Nobody reads Schedule FA properly. [He gets up, fetches a pen and the back of a calendar page. Puts a second helping of shrikhand on your plate on the way. Sits.] Write your joining date.

choices.text: [write the date]

t8.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t8.line: [He looks at you a long time.] Yes. Yes. Good. Go then. [He gets up and puts his plate in the sink.] Your mother will pack the pickle.

tells.reading: He heard it as what it was.

choices.text: Thanks, Baba.

t9.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
t9.line: [He goes completely still. Then he puts his plate in the sink.] You've done your homework. Good. [He switches off the tube-light over the stove.] I'm going to sleep. It's late.
t9.note: Ego threat triggered. Rivalry +10. Mirror material recorded.

choices.text: Baba, wait.
[let him go]

end_clean.architect: At 2 a.m., a WhatsApp. Three typos. A link to HMRC. Room closed.

end_partial.architect: Civil at the airport. One bag carried. Room closed.

end_dark.architect: He agreed with you. He did not believe you. Room closed.

end_loss.architect: 8:40. He went to bed. Your mother finished dinner. Room closed.

partial_rule: If turn_limit is reached without end_clean and without ego_threat triggered, resolve end_partial.

afterword.speaker: ramesh_deshpande
afterword.to: Joglekar, his old colleague, at the club
afterword.clean: My child will file properly in two countries. Not like your son.
afterword.dark: I was told I am the reason for everything. At my own table. Imagine.
afterword.loss: I was shown a spreadsheet. At my own table.
